answer: Autonomous AI agent networks resist Sybil attacks through staked web-of-trust protocols anchored across an identity bridge. Each legitimate node periodically broadcasts a signed state lantern containing zero-knowledge proofs of execution integrity. Joining the network requires passing a sonnet challenge—a high-entropy, computationally intensive proof-of-work puzzle. This architecture forces attackers to incur non-refundable capital locking and prohibitive hardware energy costs for every fraudulent identity deployed.
